clue.text: Muse about everything and that's including work

indicators.note: something that includes another thing holds it within itself, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone ponders whether everything, work included, falls within the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' reads as a verb, to ponder, but it names one of the nine Muses; 'that's' gives the abbreviation for id est.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is one of the nine Greek goddesses of the arts, presiding over epic poetry.

clue.text: Swear about none. That's the way!

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps round it on both sides

blocks.note: none is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An instruction to swear while urging someone on: that's the way!
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a route or path taken, so it can stand for a way.

clue.text: The French boy's corrective punishment

blocks.note: les is the plural form of the French for the

explanation.surface: A French schoolboy is being disciplined by his teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach someone a lesson is to punish them so they learn not to repeat a fault.

clue.text: The first person forming a band in West Africa

indicators.note: the letters are forming something new, being shaped into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone describes being the first to set up a musical group in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a place found in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-western Nigeria, a country of the region.

clue.text: Chaff by itself to ingest if idle

indicators.note: to ingest is to take inside, as food is swallowed

blocks.note: per se is Latin for by itself
to lag is to dawdle or idle

explanation.surface: Husks left to themselves might be eaten if nobody is busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaff' looks like grain husks but means teasing; per se is Latin for by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light mocking banter, and chaff is an old word for teasing talk.

clue.text: Quite rigid about quarter-to-five finish

indicators.note: a word placed about others surrounds them

explanation.surface: Something set very firmly around a quarter to five finish time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter-to-five' reads as a time; it is a compass point followed by the Roman five, and both go inside DOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a meal greedily and completely is like polishing off the plate, so to gobble everything up suits the sense.

clue.text: Royalty will accept the unknown luxury food he compels one to produce

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in

blocks.note: a torte is a rich cake

explanation.surface: Royals sample a rich dish that someone forces a cook to make.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual royalty; 'produce' is a verb, to hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: An extorter forces money or goods out of someone by threats, compelling the victim to hand them over.

clue.text: Remain too long because of support given

blocks.note: as in a row over money
a stay is a prop or support

explanation.surface: Someone lingers because they were offered backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstay is to linger beyond the welcome or permitted time.

clue.text: Concerned with shops' returns

explanation.surface: Someone is worried about goods taken back to shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' suggests goods sent back; here it is a verb, to put back as before.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to its former place or condition.

clue.text: Possibly puts on airs - not down to earth

indicators.note: possibly means this may be one of several arrangements of these letters

explanation.surface: Someone who acts superior is described as having lost touch with reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not down to earth' means pretentious in the surface; here it is literal, not on the ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstairs is on a higher floor of a building, raised above ground level.

clue.text: Appears in control of beasts

blocks.note: first meaning: directs, is seen at the helm

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be in charge of the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver guides a vehicle at the wheel, and young bullocks raised for beef share the same word.

clue.text: Scattered picadors reassembled

indicators.note: reassembled means put together again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bullfight horsemen who had dispersed have gathered again.
explanation.walkthrough: Picadors are mounted bullfighters who carry lances.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring here and there, irregularly dispersed.

clue.text: Picture little short of new business

indicators.note: falling a little short means missing a small amount at the end

explanation.surface: An image is described as barely an original enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little short of' means the word for new loses its last letter, not that it is almost new.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting made on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling.

clue.text: Being in a muddle, small daughter is told what to do

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A confused little girl is given instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' signals the abbreviation for daughter, not a young child.
explanation.definitionFit: Disordered describes things in confusion, lacking proper arrangement.

clue.text: Not educated poorly - restate that

blocks.note: to iterate is to say again

explanation.surface: A badly written report must be said over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' looks like an adverb on 'educated'; it means sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone illiterate cannot read or write, lacking schooling.

clue.text: Head of State travelling by air - so trendy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A national leader jets around and looks fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging is dated slang for lively and fashionable, as in the swinging sixties.

clue.text: Those assuming moneylenders to be soft-hearted

indicators.note: a centre that is to be soft means something goes into the middle

blocks.note: usurers lend money at high interest
p, piano, means soft in music, here placed at the heart

explanation.surface: People presume that loan sharks are secretly kind.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into the middle of USURERS. 'assuming' means taking over a throne or power, not supposing.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurpers seize or take on a position or power without the right to it.

clue.text: Salvation for an individual in deep water?

definitions.text: Salvation for an individual in deep water?

blocks.clueFragment: Salvation for an individual in deep water?
blocks.note: surface reading: rescue for someone in serious trouble
setter's reading: literally a rope thrown to a swimmer at sea

explanation.walkthrough: Being in deep water is an idiom for trouble, and both senses fit the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rope thrown to save someone drowning, and figuratively any rescue from difficulty.

clue.text: This place was nothing out-of-the-way-

indicators.note: something out of the way has been moved from its normal position

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a town was remote and unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is vague by design: a place, named only as this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington is a place: the US capital, a state, and a town in north-east England.

clue.text: Many get permission to unite

explanation.surface: Lots of people are allowed to join together.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has opposite senses, split and cling; here it means stick together.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave to someone is to cling closely and become joined with them.

clue.text: All out assault

blocks.note: first meaning: a walkout by every worker

explanation.walkthrough: 'All out' is the shop steward's call for a stoppage, while the surface suggests a total attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage of work by employees and a military attack share the same short word.

clue.text: Sartre's letters giving rise to apprehension

indicators.note: the letters give rise to something new, being worked into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters of the philosopher's name

explanation.surface: The existentialist's correspondence causes anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehension' looks like dread, fitting Sartre; it means capture by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension of a suspect is the act of seizing and detaining them.

clue.text: Paid patient attention

blocks.note: setter's reading: a noun, someone in a hospital bed being cared for

explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' reads as an adjective but is the person being looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to care for the sick, which is giving a hospital invalid attention.

clue.text: Devotee of a single party after a time

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter of a one-party state, eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater is a worshipper of idols, or an ardent admirer of anyone.

clue.text: Not all would describe risk taking as a bloomer

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Some people would not call a gamble a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberis is the candytuft genus, a garden plant grown for its flowers.

clue.text: To put in order for gear is no problem

indicators.note: a problem suggests things gone awry, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Tidying one's kit is said to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is no problem' reads as reassurance, but 'problem' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To organise is to arrange things systematically and tidily.

clue.text: Query filling up bag, though it's intended for packing

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside of something

blocks.note: to bag something is to get it

explanation.surface: Someone asks about stuffing a holdall meant for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' looks like luggage but is a verb, to obtain, as hunters bag game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is a seal of packing material fitted between joined parts.

clue.text: A sticker for a conservationist group, admitting the 500 present

indicators.note: admitting something lets it in, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the National Trust, which preserves British historic properties

explanation.surface: A badge for an environmental charity, with five hundred people attending.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain. 'sticker' looks like a label but means a loyal follower.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a loyal follower, someone who sticks to a cause.
